newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open up after Dow advance.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open up after Dow advance.

text.p: Australian shares resumed their climb into record territory on Tuesday after Wall Street posted solid gains on Monday, fueled by rising oil prices.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 13.9 points higher at 2,377.2.
The December share price index was up nine points at 2,400 and at a 22.8 point premium to the underlying index.

Brokers said there was solid buying support for bellwether resource issues BHP, CRA as well as for the banking sector, following the announcement of a merger proposal for regional banks St George and Advance on Monday.
At 11.45 a.m. (0145 GMT), BHP shares were 22 cents higher at A$17.06 (US$13.50), while CRA shares were 33 cents higher at A$20.05.

"I expect the market will go higher after its usual mid-morning pause but I doubt it will end up a huge amount because of its strong run yesterday," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at brokerage Intersuisse.

Sekely said Wall Street's rally on Monday would not necessarily be fully reflected by the Australian market today, especially as a number of market commentators had recently been making cautionary comments about a possible Dow pullback.
"It doesn't always follow that if the Dow rises 40 points the All Ordinaries should rise 20 points," Sekely said. "But overall positive factors outweigh negative ones today."
The shares of transport group TNT were among the most active early. Traders said the company's suitor, Dutch postal and telecoms group KPN, was the main buyer.
At 11.45 a.m. (0145 GMT), TNT shares were two cents higher at A$2.42 on turnover of 26.6 million shares.
